title: Sector 3 is THE CANYON, SOL-82's first use: a canyon cut at the antipode fills with five sector pulses of the swarm, SOL-82's first pass comes over it with 45 s overhead, 25 s of burn and a 12 m beam, the player glides into its seat, and what it misses walks to the base
context: Owner, 2026-10-01: "The SOL usage is not fun; does not stay long enough, not accessible enough, not meaningful enough. let's have it used the first time at the antipode, far from all other sentries; a huge number of ennemies, 5x the usual, in a long canyon, easy target for the SOL. a satisfying use of its immense power." Asked, he chose sector 3, survivors marching on the base, an auto-seat with a glide, and the canyon pass special (every later pass is longer since 2026-10-01-sol82-every-pass-longer). The antipode is 2.4 km of arc from the base, a maze of rock and floor 254 hops from the heart; no long straight corridor exists there.
outcome: src/domain/canyon.js (new) plans it: at the heart's antipode, along whichever of 16 bearings puts its mouth on ground walked from the heart nearest it, open ground 1.2 cells either side of a 48-cell centre line, 3 cells of rock beyond and across the deep end; the programme host cuts it (one rebuild). SECTORS[2] is THE CANYON: one gate breach and canyon: true. src/fx/sector-run.js cuts it as the sector begins and puts a breach at the deep end that opens quietly (no dive: the glide is the reveal) and that nothing seals (td-tab's laser list skips obj.userData.keep), and sends one wave: CANYON.swarm (5) two-breach pulses of the ladder wave two past the sector's start, at once, drawn at 0.35 of a body's dots (hundreds of full clouds packed under the seat's camera took the frame from 60 to 18 fps). The frame budget does not weigh the swarm against the base's pulses. Once it is all up and has had 6 s, the programme host's canyonPass lays SOL-82's pass over it (src/fx/laser-arsenal.js passOver: its own overhead, energy, radius and slew for one pass, the contact on the canyon, forward along its axis, no range call; the next close restores the game's pass) and the station seats the player without the briefing. Every entry to and exit from SOL-82's seat now glides (td-tab's enter and leave; a paused game snaps instead, as before), and src/fx/seat-glide.js travels round the sphere when the two eyes are far apart (3.2 s). The base's own breach waits for the pass's overhead to end: with the player in the seat the towers alone lost the colony 35 s into the sector (measured). Isao's canyon_rises and canyon_pass. SOL-82's BUILDING LOST toast moved into src/fx/laser-station.js to pay for the controller's share.
alternatives: Bake the canyon into the story planet: changes the pinned kernel recipe and the baked planet for one sector's set piece; the runtime cut costs one rebuild (about 3 ms).
Keep the gate breach running through the pass: measured, the colony fell while the player burned.
Full-detail bodies: 18 fps under the seat's camera.
evidence: test/canyon.mjs (new): at the antipode, floor in rock, mouth on reachable ground, the deep end walks to the heart once cut. test/seat-glide.mjs (new): round the sphere, never through it, then on the goal. test/sector-run.mjs: the cut, the quiet unsealable breach, the swarm's size, scatter and density, the base's breach held until the pass is over, the pass's own numbers. test/sectors.mjs: the climb around the canyon, the swarm in the hundreds.

Browser --canyon (new): ?skip=defence&sector=3 cuts the canyon, about 375 rise, the canyon pass seats the player through a glide with the 12 m beam and 25 s; the beam walked down the canyon burned 193 to 195 in 25 s at a median 16.7 ms frame (p95 33 ms); the colony holds (10/10) and 180 walk on. --laser-game, --seats (a leave read when the glide back lands), --phone, --showcase, --sectors, --skip-tutorial green.
